clue.text: Sort of pronoun, one in a family

definitions.meaning: words like who, which and that, introducing a clause, belong to this grammatical class
a kinsman or kinswoman, someone connected by blood or marriage

explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names who and which by this term, and in everyday speech it means a family member or kin.

clue.text: Contracts: stewards get only one right

indicators.note: the stewards' word has two of the letter for right, and keeping only one means dropping the other

parts.note: pursers are the officers who look after passengers on a ship

explanation.surface: A note on employment terms: stewards are being given only one entitlement under their contracts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a noun about jobs, but it is a verb: puckers or draws together.
explanation.definitionFit: To purse the lips is to draw them tight, so the verb is a synonym of puckers or tightens.

clue.text: Applying energy, join together part of watch

indicators.note: energy is applied, stuck on the end of the joining word

parts.note: to fuse things is to join them together
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Instructions for a watch repair: apply energy and join the parts together.
explanation.walkthrough: A fusee is the cone-shaped pulley in old watches and clocks that evens out the spring's pull.
explanation.definitionFit: This cone-shaped grooved pulley carries the chain in a mechanical timepiece, a component of the movement.

clue.text: Obsessive chap, an adherent of heresy

parts.note: manic means frantic or obsessive in behaviour
a chap is a male, referred to as he
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fanatical man turns out to be a follower of some heretical creed.
explanation.walkthrough: Manichaeism, a dualist faith of light and darkness founded by Mani, was condemned by the early Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Mani's dualist creed were branded heretics by Christian orthodoxy, so a member is a heresy's adherent.

clue.text: Cut back green feature on both sides of motorway

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: the facial feature is split so that its parts stand either side of the road

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: An environmental scheme for verges planted on both sides of a motorway is cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green feature' reads as one phrase about verges, but green and feature are separate pieces; the M1 is written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to spend less, a synonym for cutting back on costs.

clue.text: Performing school run, one sends out signals

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A drama school's run is described as something sending out signals.
explanation.definitionFit: This detection system works by emitting radio pulses and reading their echoes, so it is a signal transmitter.

clue.text: Very keen to swap hands; one bridge player is not so soft

indicators.note: right is exchanged for left, the two hands, in the keen word

parts.note: ardent means passionate, very keen
East is one of the four bridge positions, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A keen bridge player switches hands and plays a firmer game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swap hands' turns R (right) into L (left), making ALDENT. Al dente describes pasta cooked to stay firm to the bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian cookery term for pasta left firm to the bite, hence not overcooked or mushy.

clue.text: Losing a pound, not so hard to affect a smile

indicators.note: the pound sign's letter is dropped from the easier word

parts.note: simpler means less hard, easier
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost a pound finds it easier to manage a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: To simper is to smile in an affected, coy way, so the verb means putting on a smile.

clue.text: A group of notes heard to be in harmony

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a chord is a group of notes played together

explanation.surface: A chord, a group of notes, sounds in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, accord means agree or be consistent, sitting in agreement with something.

clue.text: How flocks of birds often fly, wheeling in plain

indicators.note: a bird wheeling turns round, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.words: How flocks of birds often fly
parts.note: geese and other flocks fly all in a V formation

explanation.surface: Birds in a flock fly in formation, wheeling over a plain.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase ALL IN A V read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is slang for plain or ordinary, with nothing added, like the basic ice-cream flavour.

clue.text: Marine-style wake-up call?

parts.note: the French phrase meaning in the manner of someone, used in English
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A bugle reveille in the manner of the Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: Marine-style means in the manner of the Royal Marines: in French form, à la RM.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm clock or signal rouses sleepers, so this device gives a call to get up.

clue.text: Trunk for senior manager to tour islands

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: touring something means going around it, so the manager's word surrounds the islands

parts.note: a boss is a senior manager
CI is short for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A trunk of luggage for a senior executive's tour of some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long nose is its proboscis, the anatomical name for a trunk.

clue.text: Deal with trauma — ask for Indian manual

indicators.note: dealing out cards mixes them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to someone traumatised: ask for an Indian self-help book.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Sanskrit text on love and sex is a famous treatise from India, a handbook or guide.

clue.text: Four characters from bard, old hat

indicators.note: only the first four letters of the poet's name are kept

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Four characters from a Shakespeare play wear an old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A shako is a tall, peaked military hat with a plume.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a cylindrical military cap, a type of headgear.

clue.text: Cut down similar colours — no pressure

parts.note: red and puce are similar reddish colours

indicators.note: no pressure means the letter for pressure is taken away

parts.note: red and puce are similar reddish colours
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Advice to tone down similar colours and not apply pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes P from REDPUCE to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce is to lessen or make smaller, a synonym of cutting down.

clue.text: Corps avoided marching? Fit for use again, then

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps
soldiers who cycled went by bike rather than marching

explanation.surface: Army engineers skipped the march by bike, so they were fit to serve again.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycled material has been processed for reuse, made usable a second time.

clue.text: Identify large tree that's fallen over, one shooting

indicators.note: something fallen over lies the other way, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to name someone is to identify them
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
a fir is a conifer tree

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to identify a big tree that has toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's fallen over' turns NAME + L + FIR back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is a soldier armed with a rifle, someone who shoots.

clue.text: With girl, love is a snare

indicators.note: the zero for love goes along with the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
love means nil in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A sentimental line: with a girl, love is a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope for catching animals, a kind of snare or trap.

clue.text: Show original touches of nudism

indicators.note: original means novel or new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre show features innovative touches of nakedness.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of 'touches of nudism' rearrange into the musical's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodgers and Hammerstein's stage musical about the von Trapp family, a famous theatre production.

clue.text: What Britain once had originally replaced by Virginia, fabulous creature

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is swapped out for the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Britain once ruled an empire
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Britain's former empire in America was replaced by Virginia, a creature of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire is a mythical bloodsucking monster, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Merely innocuous, but sacked on the spot

indicators.note: sacked in the sense of ransacked, with the letters thrown about

explanation.surface: A harmless worker is fired abruptly with no fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Done unceremoniously means abruptly, without formality, as if on the spot.

clue.text: Planting way below ground to come up, grow bigger flower

indicators.note: planting puts one thing into another, here into the growing word

parts.note: to swell is to grow bigger

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: deep means far below the surface

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a bulb deep so that it comes up and grows into a big flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' reads the way-below-ground word upwards, and 'Planting' sets it inside the growing word, as a bulb goes into soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell, or veronica, is a small blue-flowered plant.

clue.text: Guard small door …

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
an entry is a doorway or way in

explanation.surface: A guard is posted at a small door.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier on guard duty, a lookout.

clue.text: if not more?

parts.note: read as ..., not less, which is what more means

explanation.surface: The ellipsis continues the guard's door: if not, more?
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 8 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless is a conjunction meaning except if, so it stands in for if not.

clue.text: Pronounced demand thus withdrawn?

parts.note: the prefix de- means removed or taken back
claimed means demanded as of right

explanation.surface: Someone's demand is announced and then retracted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as de-claimed, a claim taken back.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak out forcefully, so declaimed means pronounced or recited.

clue.text: Send message, one maybe stolen by 21

definitions.meaning: to ... is to send a message along
a secret login that the security-bypassing intruder of 21 down might steal

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means relay a message; as one, it is a secret login code that a cracker could take.

clue.text: Not the principal task to file record

indicators.note: filing a record puts it away inside something, here inside the task

parts.note: a duty is a task
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A task: filing a record for a junior staffer.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy acts for someone more senior, a second-in-command rather than the chief.

clue.text: Disregard member of orchestra, extremely tiresome

parts.note: a viola is an instrument in an orchestra's string section

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of tiresome are used

explanation.surface: An orchestra player, extremely tiresome, is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a rule is to break it, showing disregard for it.

clue.text: PM on TV who bypasses security measures?

definitions.meaning: The Prime Minister in the BBC sitcom Yes, Prime Minister
someone who breaks into computer systems

explanation.definitionFit: Jim Hacker was the fictional premier in a BBC comedy, and the word also means a computer intruder.

clue.text: Crop left to progress slowly

parts.note: a craw is a bird's crop, the pouch in its gullet

explanation.surface: A crop left in the field grows slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to move along very slowly, inching forward.
